requirements.goal: Build the native game-core module (ADR-019/roadmap #4): ECS, collision, tilemap loading, sprite-animation timing, bought crates (bevy_ecs or hecs, rapier2d, glam, tiled), rendering via gfx/* draw batches.
requirements.constraints: Follow ADR-011/017 Module trait contract and audio module as the structural template; no rendering authority of its own (turns state into gfx/* batches); modules never depend on other modules crates; kernel/headless build unaffected; one-type-per-file + out-of-line tests + crate README per docs/code-style.md.
requirements.done: A minimal 2D scene simulates entities with collision on a loaded tilemap, rendered through gfx/*, demonstrated via a runnable example extension.
requirements.outOfScope: gfx/* rendering authority, sprite-animation asset pipeline beyond timing state machine, physics beyond 2D collision, any change to renderer ownership of the window surface.

increments.description: New core/game-core crate added to the workspace: Cargo.toml with hecs, rapier2d, glam deps; GameCore struct implementing bus::Module + Handler (empty subscribe/handle for now); crate README stub. Proves the new deps compile and link into the workspace.

hecs World owned by GameCore; a game-core/spawn-entity bus command creates entities with transform + sprite-animation components; on core/tick, animation frame-index-from-elapsed-time state machine advances. Unit tests cover spawn and frame advance.

rapier2d physics pipeline steps alongside the ECS on core/tick; entities can carry a collider component; post-step positions sync back into transform components. Unit tests cover two colliding bodies resolving overlap.

game-core/load-tilemap bus command carries map bytes; tiled parses it; a designated collision layer becomes static rapier2d colliders at load time. Unit test covers a small fixture map producing the expected collider count/positions.

GameCore turns ECS transforms/sprite-animation frames into gfx::SetCamera + gfx::DrawSprite batches published each tick; new extensions/game_core_demo WASM extension spawns a few colliding entities on a loaded tilemap; app config gains a game_core toggle. Demo: the scene visibly simulates entities colliding on the tilemap through gfx/*.

SpawnEntity gains an application-assigned entity id; new game-core/set-velocity command lets a caller drive a spawned entitys rapier2d velocity directly (both dynamic and kinematic bodies keep working). game_core_demo gains WASD + gamepad-left-stick movement for one entity and several additional static obstacles on the level tilemap to collide against. Demo: moving the controlled entity into obstacles/other entities visibly blocks it.

increments.scope: gfx Clear + open-closed entity-op wire API
increments.description: game-core publishes gfx::Clear every tick before drawing sprites, fixing the retained-batch smearing and invisible-obstacle bug. game-core/spawn-entity and game-core/set-velocity collapse into one game-core/entity-op topic carrying a tagged EntityOp enum (Spawn, SetVelocity, Despawn), following ui::Spec/Widget precedent so future entity operations extend the enum without a new topic. load-tilemap stays its own topic (one-shot asset load, not a per-entity op). Demo updated to the new API; visually verified clean (no smear) with obstacles visible.

increments.scope: fix sprite draw-position offset from collider center
increments.description: DrawSprite currently uses transform.x/y (the rapier2d collider center) directly as dst_x/dst_y (DrawSprite top-left), while DrawRect already correctly converts center to top-left for squares. Fix publish_gfx so DrawSprite subtracts half frame_w/frame_h the same way, so a sprite entitys visible art lines up with its actual collider extent and contact with obstacles looks correct. Demo: the robot visibly touches and stops against the red squares at the same point its hitbox does, verified live.

game-core tracks tilemap-loaded fixed colliders as their own entities (or a lightweight parallel list) carrying a Transform + SquareColor, so publish_gfx draws them as gfx::DrawRect squares alongside spawned entities. Fixes demo legibility: the interior maze walls that were invisible (correct collision, no visual) now render, so what looked like a bug ("invisible wall") is visibly a wall. Verified live: the level.tmx interior walls appear as squares matching where movement is actually blocked.

level.tmx keeps only its outer boundary walls (object ids 1-4); the interior plus-shaped maze walls (object ids 5-7) are removed so the controlled entity can freely reach all obstacle squares from its spawn point without needing to navigate around walls. Demo: the robot can path directly to every red obstacle square.

EntityOp::Spawn gains a body_kind (Dynamic/Kinematic) alongside collider_half_w/h; Kinematic uses RigidBodyBuilder::kinematic_velocity_based (moves via set-velocity, pushes dynamics on contact, never pushed itself). SpriteAnimation only advances when its entitys collider has nonzero rapier2d linear velocity (near-zero freezes on the current frame) -- derived internally, no new wire message. Unit tests cover a kinematic body pushing a dynamic one without itself being displaced, and animation freezing/resuming based on velocity.

GameCore installs a rapier2d EventHandler to collect CollisionEvent::Started for collider pairs where both colliders belong to hecs entities tracked in self.entities (ignoring tilemap colliders). Each such contact publishes a new game-core/collision message carrying both entity_ids. Unit test spawns two overlapping dynamic entities and asserts a collision event with both ids is published exactly once per new contact (not every tick while overlapping).

EntityOp gains SetColor { entity_id, color }: overwrites an existing SquareColor components color in place (no-op for an unknown entity_id or one with no SquareColor, e.g. a sprite entity). Lets a caller implement a temporary color flash (set, wait, set back) without needing game-core to know about hit-flash timing itself. Unit tests cover a successful color change and both no-op cases.

increments.scope: demo: blue kinematic squares, footstep audio, hit-flash + sound
increments.description: game_core_demo spawns two blue Kinematic obstacle squares alongside the existing red Dynamic ones. The extension enables core/audio, synthesizes two short WAV tones (footstep click, hit blip) in code, and: plays the footstep tone on a fixed interval while its own held-input velocity is nonzero; subscribes to game-core/collision and, on an event naming two red obstacle entity_ids, publishes a brief SquareColor override (a new EntityOp op or SetVelocity-adjacent mechanism) for 0.1-0.5s plus the hit tone. Demo: moving the robot produces footstep sound only while moving and only while the sprite is animating; a red square driven into another red square flashes color and plays a sound.
